info.title: Ray'z Barber Shop API
info.description:
Public booking + customer API used by rayzbs.com booking pages and the future iOS/Android app.

**Auth:** customers sign in with a one-time code (SMS or email) → `accessToken` (JWT, 1 hour) + rotating `refreshToken` (60 days).
Send `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`. Refresh with `POST /auth/refresh`; reusing an old refresh token revokes all sessions.

**Time:** every shop runs on America/Chicago. Dates are local `YYYY-MM-DD`; instants are ISO-8601 UTC.
**Money:** integer cents. **Privacy:** barbers are exposed by first name / admin label only; URLs never contain surnames.
**Retries:** `POST /appointments` honors an `Idempotency-Key` header so a flaky mobile network can't double-book.

**App builds:** send `X-Client: ios|android` and `X-App-Version: 1.2.3` on every request. A build below the platform's minimum gets `426` with `error.code = upgrade_required` and `details.storeUrl` on every route except `GET /app/config` and this document. Requests without `X-Client` (the website) are never gated.

**Changes in 1.1 (additive):** `GET /app/config`; `bookingMode` and `externalBookingUrl` on shops (send clients to the external URL while a shop still books on its old site); `preferences` on `/me` with `preferencesNote` and `preferredBarberId` on `PATCH /me`; the `upgrade_required` error code.

**Changes in 1.2:** a sign-in code no longer lists the profiles on a number (`chooseProfile` is never returned; treat it like `needsProfile` and ask for a first name). New sign-in steps: `stepUp` (a number unused 18 months confirms with the profile's verified email via `/auth/step-up/*`) and `cantSignIn` (offer `POST /auth/help`). `identityCheckRequired` on tokens and `/me`, with `POST /me/identity-check`; `redemptionLocked` on `/me/loyalty`. Only a verified email signs in: `emailVerified` on `/me`, and a new email goes through `/me/email/start` and `/me/email/verify` (`PATCH /me` only clears it). `appHash` on `/auth/otp/start` for Android. `features` (kill switches) on `/app/config`; a switched-off feature answers 403 with `details.switch`. Code requests are limited per IP as well as per number (429 with `details.retryAfterSeconds`). Account deletion: `GET /me/delete` (what happens), `POST /me/delete/start` (code), `POST /me/delete`; `links` on `/app/config` adds `support` and `deleteAccount` (the web page, which works without the app), and privacy and terms default to pages on this site. Consent: `GET`/`PUT /me/consent` (appointment and marketing texts, emails and app push, each recorded with the wording's version), the four new flags on `/me`, and push devices at `/me/devices`. Sessions: `GET /me/sessions` (where I'm signed in), `DELETE /me/sessions` (everywhere else) and `DELETE /me/sessions/{id}`; signing out or ending a session stops its access token at once and revokes the push devices registered in it. Receipts: `receiptDelivery` on `/me` (email or app; a counter checkout then sends the receipt with nothing asked), `GET /me/receipts` and `/me/receipts/{id}`, and a push with `data.kind = receipt`. Cards and paying in the app: `/me/payment-methods` (saved cards on a platform-level Stripe Customer, set up with `POST /me/payment-methods/setup` for PaymentSheet), tickets the shop sends to the app at `/me/tickets` (push `data.kind = ticket`), the card fee before authorizing with `POST /me/tickets/{id}/quote` (credit cards only, worked out server-side from the card's funding type; re-quote when the payment method changes; the ticket's `cardFee` adds `type`, `flatCents`, `capCents`, `minCents`, `wallets` and `off`, and `feeReason` adds `channel_off`, `state_not_allowed` and `waived`), and `POST /me/tickets/{id}/pay` (`requires_action` for 3-D Secure); `payments` on `/app/config`. Accounts: the app books signed in (401 `sign_in_required` otherwise) and signed-out website bookings never join an existing profile until that phone signs in; account holders are 13 or older (`ageConfirmed` on `/auth/otp/verify` and `/auth/otp/complete`, required from the app; `accounts` on `/app/config`); `PUT /me/secure` (`secured` on `/me`, and `stepUp.reason` is `secured` for such a profile); `POST /me/family/claim`; the family endpoints (`/me/family`, children, family bookings and booking groups; 403 `details.switch = family` when switched off), `/me/badges` and the public `/locations`; `/me/appointments` pages (`status`, `cursor`, `limit`, `family`, and `nextCursor`); `GET /me/loyalty/ledger`; `GET /me/suggested-rebook`; `policies` on `GET /shops/{shop}`; `homeShop` and `birthday` on `/me` (set with `homeShopId` and `birthday` on `PATCH /me`); a child (dependent) keeps a first name and birth year only (`birthYear` on family members; their `lastName`, `birthday` and `photo` are always null).

post.summary: Book an appointment
post.description: The app (X-Client ios/android) books signed in. Signed-out booking is the website's: limited per IP and per phone or email, behind Cloudflare Turnstile when it's on, never added to an existing profile until the phone signs in with a code, and at most one confirmation text a day to a number nobody has verified. With a barber who books with a card on file, the app needs a saved card on the household's account (the guardian's for a child).

403.description: Booking is switched off (details.switch); under 13 (under_13); the bot check failed (bot_check_required, bot_check_failed); no saved card for a barber who needs one (card_required)

429.description: Too many guest bookings from this network or for this phone

post.description: One adult profile on this phone (or verified email): tokens, unless the number has been unused for 18 months (`stepUp` or `cantSignIn`). None or several: `{needsProfile: true, selectionToken}`; ask for a first name and finish with /auth/otp/complete (the code isn't needed again). Who else is on a number is never shown. Sending firstName here does the same matching up front.

post.description: Creates a task for staff. With a selectionToken (the number was proven with a code) the profiles on it are attached for staff; they're never shown to the caller.

post.summary: Delete the account with a fresh code
post.description: Deletes only the chosen profile (and, for your own, your children's). Other adults on the same phone are untouched. The profile is anonymized: contact details, notes, photo, preferences, sessions and upcoming bookings go; past tickets stay under "Deleted client" for accounting. Every token for it stops working.

post.summary: Make a child's profile on my phone number my dependent (I15)
post.description: For a child the shop has as their own profile on the parent's phone. Done at once when the shop's record shows them under 13 and the profile was never used on its own; otherwise the shop checks first (status requested). The profiles on a number are never listed: send the child's first name. Five tries an hour.

put.description: Marketing on each channel is its own yes, never implied by appointment texts or emails, and Squire imports never grant it. A yes needs the textVersion from GET /me/consent (400 with details.textVersion when the wording changed). A yes to marketing texts after a STOP stays blocked until the number texts START (blockedBy: stop). A yes to marketing email needs a verified email. Turning appointment notifications on (push_transactional) is how the app gets push about its bookings; register the phone with POST /me/devices too.

post.summary: The tip and the card fee for the card picked, before the client authorizes
post.description: Use PaymentSheet's FlowController: the client picks a saved card or enters one (a ConfirmationToken), this returns the fee and total from the card's funding, and your own Pay button calls /pay. Only credit cards pay the surcharge: never debit or prepaid, and not Apple Pay or Google Pay unless /app/config payments.walletFee.

post.summary: Pay the ticket
post.description: Send the card and the quote's totalCents as expectedTotalCents (409 with details.totalCents if it changed). status requires_action: run the bank's check with clientSecret (handleNextAction), then POST again with paymentIntentId. A payment that succeeds after the app closes is finished by Stripe's webhook, and the receipt arrives by push.
